reference: Bash metadata and documented pty contracts. Private regular-file descriptors independently fix the negative isatty and successful/duplicate-close outcomes. Terminal/session behavior remains deferred; no external GNU PTY API parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash type -t and type identify pty as an enabled shell builtin.
Bash help exposes the pty documentation and lists each public subcommand family.
Actual private-descriptor nonterminal classification, closure, duplicate-close error and descriptor parse rejection.
exclusions: No GNU command provides this loadable's PTY/session API; no operational parity oracle is available.

Session/TTY allocation, positive terminal classification, child PTY lifecycle and serial line-discipline behavior remain deferred. Only ordinary private-file descriptors are used by runnable operations.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must classify the statically enabled pty loadable as a builtin.
Bash type must describe pty as a shell builtin, not as an external executable.
The Bash help entry must document every public subcommand family declared by the loadable.
cases.script:
doc=$(help pty)
for text in \
  'pty setsid' \
  'pty open-tty PATH' \
  'pty isatty FD' \
  'pty tty-name FD' \
  'pty foreground PGRP' \
  'pty close FD' \
  'pty spawn FDVAR PIDVAR CMD' \
  'pty waitpid PID' \
  'pty echo FD on|off' \
  'pty resize FD' \
  'pty set-ldisc LDISC DEVICE'; do
  case $doc in
    *"$text"*) ;;
    *) exit 1 ;;
  esac
done
printf 'all documented subcommands present\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise setsid, open-tty, and foreground against a controlled session and controlling terminal.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with a private PTY/TTY fixture and session support. That fixture must verify setsid, TIOCSCTTY acquisition, FDVAR versus stdio behavior, and foreground process-group assignment without opening a host console. No controlling-terminal or session operation is run by this suite.

cases.purpose: Exercise isatty, tty-name, close, echo, and resize on a private PTY pair.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed PTY mock that provides a private master/slave pair, stable tty-name, and observable termios and winsize state. It must verify terminal classification, descriptor closure, echo toggling, geometry updates, and any SIGWINCH effect without using a host terminal. No terminal state mutation is invoked.

cases.purpose: Exercise spawn and waitpid with bounded child output, exit status, and descriptor cleanup.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private PTY driver and process namespace, or a reviewed syscall mock for PTY allocation and child handoff. A bounded fixture should run only a fixed harmless child, check master/slave wiring, captured output, exit-status propagation, repeated waits, and cleanup. This suite must not start pty spawn or waitpid operations here.

cases.purpose: Exercise set-ldisc validation and line-discipline changes against an isolated serial endpoint.
cases.reason: Requires a reviewed ioctl mock or a disposable VM with a dedicated virtual serial endpoint and narrowly scoped capability support. The future fixture must validate termios options and TIOCSETD on that virtual endpoint only; no real device or privileged operation is suitable for this runner.

cases.purpose: The assigned isatty interface classifies a private regular-file descriptor as nonterminal.
Close an explicitly opened private descriptor and verify a second close fails while the file remains intact.
cases.script:
exec 9>ordinary
printf saved >&9
pty close 9
if pty close 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'second-close=%s\n' "$rc"
exec 9<ordinary
value=$(<ordinary)
[[ $value == saved ]]
exec 9<&-

cases.purpose: Reject a nonnumeric descriptor before closing anything.
